title: Add graceful shutdown with signal handling and in‑flight request draining
description: Implement process signal listeners (SIGINT, SIGTERM) that trigger a controlled shutdown of the yantraverse server, stop accepting new connections, and wait for ongoing requests to finish or timeout. This prevents abrupt termination, protects data integrity, and improves reliability in containerized production environments.
testCases: Simulate SIGTERM while a long‑running request is in flight and verify the server stops accepting new connections but allows the request to complete before exiting
Trigger SIGINT with no active requests and confirm the server closes immediately and exits with code 0
acceptance: When the process receives SIGINT or SIGTERM, the server stops accepting new requests, waits up to 30 seconds for active requests to finish, then exits with status 0. If the timeout elapses, it forces shutdown with status 1. All unit and integration tests pass.
reason: Production deployments (Kubernetes, Docker) rely on graceful termination to avoid dropped requests and corrupted state. Adding this feature eliminates a common source of runtime errors and aligns yantraverse with best‑practice lifecycle management.
